title: Supervisory Risks and International Fund Standards
summary: The main sources of investor harm and systemic risk in funds and asset management, and how international standards and typical fund regulatory regimes are designed to mitigate them.
contentGaps: Written as part of a programme: Aim and Purpose is the module's one-line description; audience, prior knowledge and core reading come from the programme

sections.Aim and Purpose: The main sources of investor harm and systemic risk in funds and asset management, and how international standards and typical fund regulatory regimes are designed to mitigate them.
Learning Objectives: Identify the key supervisory risks in funds and asset management
Explain the IOSCO principles and standard-setter work relevant to collective investment schemes
Distinguish retail fund product rules from regimes for alternative fund managers
Syllabus: Risk mapping: conflicts, investment, liquidity, operational and conduct risk
IOSCO Objectives and Principles and the collective investment scheme standards
Product-regulated retail funds versus manager-regulated alternative funds
Workshop: mapping supervisory risk areas to the regulatory schema
Intended Audience: Supervisors, inspectors and authorisation staff responsible for fund managers, funds, depositaries and fund administrators
Policy, risk and financial stability specialists working on asset management and non-bank financial intermediation
Team leaders and heads of department setting supervisory priorities for the funds sector
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some experience of supervising or authorising asset managers or funds is helpful. No specialist investment or quantitative background is required.
Core Reading: FSB, Revised Policy Recommendations to Address Structural Vulnerabilities from Liquidity Mismatch in Open-Ended Funds (2023)
IOSCO, Recommendations for Liquidity Risk Management for Collective Investment Schemes (2018)
IOSCO, Principles for the Valuation of Collective Investment Schemes (2013)
IOSCO, Objectives and Principles of Securities Regulation (2017)
